Summary

Eight files changed (CI, tooling, e2e harness, snapshots). No bugs, regressions, security risks, or CI hazards found.

Findings

F1 — Advisory (not blocking) — package.json:31

npm run lint now runs the debt ratchet (lint-baseline.mjs) instead of strict ESLint (run-eslint.mjs). It passes as long as violation counts don't increase — it won't fail on pre-existing violations at or below baseline. Old strict behavior is preserved as npm run lint:eslint:strict.

- No CI workflow, git hook, or automated script calls bare npm run lint (verified). eslint.yml uses lint:ci.
- Impact: developer ergonomics / docs only. Not a release hazard.

Other areas verified — all clean

- eslint.yml ordering: test:eslint-runner gates before lint:ci — correct, prevents bad lint configs from passing silently.
- lint:ci double-scan: intentional whole-repo ratchet plus per-PR incremental check, chained correctly.
- hideBasemapLayers: generic MapLibre masking does not affect DeckGL layers.
- firstConflictCenter: bounding-box centroid logic and empty-coordinate guard are correct.
- apt-groups-z5 scenario: correctly wires cyberThreats and uses a stricter assertion.
- ADSB flight seed: deterministic and inert unless the adsb layer is enabled.
- eslint-baseline.test.mjs: covers summarize, fatal separation, and ratchet comparison.
- tests/lint-workflow.test.mjs: structural assertion prevents workflow-order regression.

Test gaps

None critical. The CI job exercises real ESLint on every PR.
